cd "/Users/sebastianrogg/PycharmProjects/Hackathons & Projekte/WireClaim/presentation/diagrams" && cat > pitch-architecture.puml <<'PUML'
@startuml
' WireClaim — the pitch diagram. ADR 0001 made visible.
' Deliberately simpler than docs/diagrams/03-components.puml: this one is projected
' for ~40 seconds, so it carries the ONE claim (evidence in, arithmetic out) and the
' loop that closes it, and nothing else.
!theme plain
skinparam backgroundColor #0B0C0E
skinparam shadowing false
skinparam roundCorner 10
skinparam defaultFontName "SF Mono, Menlo, Consolas, monospace"
skinparam defaultFontSize 13
skinparam defaultFontColor #E7E5E4
skinparam ArrowColor #A8A29E
skinparam ArrowFontColor #A8A29E
skinparam ArrowFontSize 11
skinparam componentStyle rectangle
skinparam linetype ortho
skinparam TitleFontSize 18
skinparam TitleFontColor #E8B84B

skinparam rectangle {
  BackgroundColor #17191C
  BorderColor #3F3F46
  FontColor #E7E5E4
}
skinparam package {
  BackgroundColor #0F1113
  BorderColor #52525B
  FontColor #A8A29E
  FontSize 12
}
skinparam database {
  BackgroundColor #17191C
  BorderColor #E8B84B
  FontColor #E7E5E4
}
skinparam note {
  BackgroundColor #1C1917
  BorderColor #E8B84B
  FontColor #D6D3D1
  FontSize 11
}

title The model reads. The engine prices.

package "  ONE CASE, 60 SECONDS  " as CasePkg {
  rectangle "policy.txt\ndescription.txt\ninvoices.pdf\n**no prices**" as Case
}

package "  EVIDENCE  —  language, never arithmetic  " as EvidencePkg {
  rectangle "**Channel A**  invoice shape\nquantity printed as \"- -\"\n⇒ p(covered) = 0" as ChA
  rectangle "**Channel B**  Price Memory\nwordings watched settle\nlog error **0.43**" as ChB
  rectangle "**Channel C**  the model\ncoverage probability +\nprice band + clause **quoted**" as ChC
}

package "  PRICING ENGINE  —  arithmetic, never language  " as EnginePkg {
  rectangle "**blend**\ninverse-variance,\nlog space" as Blend
  rectangle "**posterior over t**\n(1−p)·δ(0)  +  p·LogN(m, σ)" as Post
  rectangle "**a** = k(σ) · m\n**b** = Q⅓(posterior)" as Price
}

rectangle "SUBMIT\n(a, b) per Line Item" as Submit

database "SETTLED\nTRANSACTIONS" as Txn

package "  THE LOOP  —  why every claim is a measurement  " as LoopPkg {
  rectangle "**t-inversion**\nreject @ amount>0 ⇒ a ≤ t\nreject @ 0        ⇒ a > t" as Invert
  rectangle "**replay harness**\nall 16 rivals held fixed\nnets reproduced **to the cent**" as Replay
}

Case -down-> ChA
Case -down-> ChB
Case -down-> ChC

ChA -down-> Post : mass at 0
ChB -down-> Blend
ChC -down-> Blend
Blend -down-> Post
Post -down-> Price
Price -down-> Submit
Submit -right-> Txn : 16 opponents,\nboth roles

Txn -up-> Invert
Invert -right-> Replay
Invert -up-> ChB : new anchors
Replay -up-> Price : every constant\nis a hypothesis\nwith a falsifier

note right of Price #1C1917
  **No model output is ever a price.**
  That is the whole architecture.
  It is why a prompt can be swept,
  folded and replayed — and why
  Games 82–89 still banked +254,092
  with the model endpoint returning
  401 on every single call.
end note

@enduml

@startuml
' WireClaim — the pitch diagram. ADR 0001 made visible.
' Deliberately simpler than docs/diagrams/03-components.puml: this one is projected
' for ~40 seconds, so it carries the ONE claim (evidence in, arithmetic out) and the
' loop that closes it, and nothing else.
!theme plain
skinparam backgroundColor #0B0C0E
skinparam shadowing false
skinparam roundCorner 10
skinparam defaultFontName "SF Mono, Menlo, Consolas, monospace"
skinparam defaultFontSize 13
skinparam defaultFontColor #E7E5E4
skinparam ArrowColor #A8A29E
skinparam ArrowFontColor #A8A29E
skinparam ArrowFontSize 11
skinparam componentStyle rectangle
skinparam linetype ortho
skinparam TitleFontSize 18
skinparam TitleFontColor #E8B84B

skinparam rectangle {
  BackgroundColor #17191C
  BorderColor #3F3F46
  FontColor #E7E5E4
}
skinparam package {
  BackgroundColor #0F1113
  BorderColor #52525B
  FontColor #A8A29E
  FontSize 12
}
skinparam database {
  BackgroundColor #17191C
  BorderColor #E8B84B
  FontColor #E7E5E4
}
skinparam note {
  BackgroundColor #1C1917
  BorderColor #E8B84B
  FontColor #D6D3D1
  FontSize 11
}

title The model reads. The engine prices.

package "  ONE CASE, 60 SECONDS  " as CasePkg {
  rectangle "policy.txt\ndescription.txt\ninvoices.pdf\n**no prices**" as Case
}

package "  EVIDENCE  —  language, never arithmetic  " as EvidencePkg {
  rectangle "**Channel A**  invoice shape\nquantity printed as  - -\n⇒ p(covered) = 0" as ChA
  rectangle "**Channel B**  Price Memory\nwordings watched settle\nlog error **0.43**" as ChB
  rectangle "**Channel C**  the model\ncoverage probability +\nprice band + clause **quoted**" as ChC
  ChA -[hidden]right- ChB
  ChB -[hidden]right- ChC
}

package "  PRICING ENGINE  —  arithmetic, never language  " as EnginePkg {
  rectangle "**blend**\ninverse-variance,\nlog space" as Blend
  rectangle "**posterior over t**\n(1−p)·δ(0)  +  p·LogN(m, σ)" as Post
  rectangle "**a** = k(σ) · m\n**b** = Q⅓(posterior)" as Price
}

rectangle "SUBMIT\n(a, b) per Line Item" as Submit

database "SETTLED\nTRANSACTIONS" as Txn

package "  THE LOOP  —  why every claim is a measurement  " as LoopPkg {
  rectangle "**t-inversion**\nreject @ amount>0 ⇒ a ≤ t\nreject @ 0        ⇒ a > t" as Invert
  rectangle "**replay harness**\nall 16 rivals held fixed\nnets reproduced **to the cent**" as Replay
}

Case -down-> ChA
Case -down-> ChB
Case -down-> ChC

ChA -down-> Post : mass at 0
ChB -down-> Blend
ChC -down-> Blend
Blend -down-> Post
Post -down-> Price
Price -down-> Submit
Submit -right-> Txn : 16 opponents,\nboth roles

Txn -up-> Invert
Invert -right-> Replay
Invert -up-> ChB : new anchors
Replay -up-> Price : every constant\nis falsifiable

@enduml

# How WireClaim gets judged

Sources: **[KO]** kick-off deck, 23 pp (page refs = PDF page numbers, slides unnumbered); **[QC]** QuantCo deck, 6 pp (printed numbers match PDF pages). Cross-referenced with **[HO]** `[PUBLIC] EHL Cases/GAME_DESCRIPTION.md` and `API_HANDBOOK.md`, because the decks are explicitly a summary.

## 1. Judging criteria — no rubric exists

Four statements, that's all:

- **"Your methodology also counts (style)!"** [QC p6] — typeset as a tilted, slapped-on label over a leaderboard screenshot; the only annotation-styled element in the deck.
- **"maximize the amount of money you make"** and **"do so with style"** [HO, Your Task].
- **"We will assess your approach and look at how well it performed to determine the winner. The best teams will present their approach to us."** [HO, How to win] — leaderboard position buys the right to pitch.
- The leaderboard QuantCo chose to show has columns **`RANK | TEAM | INCOME | COSTS | NET`**, sorted by NET — and three of six demo teams sit at `INCOME 0.00 / COSTS 3247.38`, i.e. the organisers' own illustration is a dark team being farmed (our R10).

**The closest thing to a rubric is [KO p21] "building a convincing winning pitch"**: `1) The solution` — "Break down your unique idea / What makes it fundamentally different?"; `2) The Demo` — "Show the product solving the problem / How would we use your solution?"; `3) The proof` — "Show us metrics, results, benchmarks or anything else to make us believe in you / Why are you the best?" Three cards, three deck sections.

**Two juries:** challenge setters/"our judges" at 12:30, the cross-partner **"hack council"** at 14:15 [KO p16, p19]. **Two prizes:** *quantco track* 1000 € plus per-person AirPods Pro 3 + 100 € agent credit; overall 1st = 1500 € + 2500 $ OpenAI credits [KO p15, QC p6].

## 2. Pitch format

**"5min pitching & demo presentation" | "3min jury questions"**, Sunday 12:30, three parallel sessions. Two rules, verbatim: **"kiss (keep it short and simple), only use slides submitted on ehl.gg."** Finalists repeat on the main stage at 14:15. Rooms come from Discord — a *hidden* leftover text box on [KO p19] (48 pt Manrope, sitting under the navy card) reads "Challenge 2; room palo", so the convention is `Challenge N; room <name>`.

**The binding constraint:** submission deadline 12:00, first pitch 12:30. The deck must be uploaded before the deadline and cannot be edited after — while our Game 100 settles at 11:50. Any final number on stage needs a one-command script, or the deck quotes Game 99 and says so.

## 3. Write-up requirement

**Not in either PDF.** Only [HO]: "you are asked to provide a **small write-up of your strategy**." The decks add channel and deadline only — submit on ehl.gg, Sunday 12:00 — plus **"The notion page is the single source of truth"** [KO p18]. The exact form fields live on Notion and nothing in this repo has captured them; someone should open that guide well before 12:00.

## 4. Rules & notation

Neither PDF has the payoff table, the Cap, or a formula — [QC p5] says **"More details can be found on our handout!"**. Report quotes the handout's payoff table, the `c ≥ 4t` cap paragraph, the fair/fraud number line and the worked example verbatim.

Two things to fix in how we cite: **the 3× weighting of the last 20 Games appears in no organiser PDF** (mid-tournament announcement — `docs/methodology-full.md:260`), and **[QC p4] says "New case released every 10 minutes"** against our measured 757.575758 s. Also absent from both decks: the 100-Game count, the schedule window, and any team count.

## 5. Guidance on a good solution

Demo is expected inside the 5 minutes. Entire is a hard gate: **"If you do not use Entire, your submissions will be rejected"** [KO p16]. The event's premise is agentic (Codex talk, Devin workshop). Highest-leverage framing available: **QuantCo's own product stack on [QC p2] is four layers — Intake / Claims Agents & Statistical Modelling / Human In the Loop Workplace / Enablement & Integration Layer** — mapping our architecture onto those four tells the challenge setters we built a piece of their roadmap. Also worth one line: our leaderboard-inversion work sits next to the handout's "extract the secret thresholds" prohibition, and we have explicit clearance (R9) — say we asked.

## 6. Branding

**QuantCo:** black/white, dotted-grid ground, **Familjen Grotesk** headlines, **Courier New for the symbols `a`/`b`/`t`, set in green `#188038`**, banner green `#5ACC9A`, fair-zone gradient `#E0F5EC`→`#63CE9F`, fraud-zone `#E78C8C`→`#F6D9D9`, thin outline rounded cards, `quantco Q | N` lockup bottom-right.

**EHL:** off-white `#EFEFEF` ground (never pure white), **Manrope** all-lowercase headlines, navy `#0A0630`/`#272448`, purple `#AC78FF` / `#9A64D9` / `#634098`, pill bars and rounded cards, alert red `#FF3131` used exactly once. EHL wordmark in Horizon-Bold inside EU stars; mascot is a pixel-art Münchner Kindl with a Monster can.

Bucket items by what they turned out to be worth and strictness pays 9.9 : 1 under €100 and loses above €500 — a compelling case for raising the Limit on expensive items.

Bucket by t̂, the only split knowable at submission time, and the gradient collapses. Of 23 items we believed were worth over 2,000, 14 turned out to be worth under half that.

Per Line Item we submit a Charge `a` and an acceptance Limit `b` against a secret fair value `t`.
Every number below is reproducible from a script in this repository; the deeper version is
[`docs/METHODOLOGY.md`](docs/METHODOLOGY.md), and the appendix with every table is
[`docs/methodology-full.md`](docs/methodology-full.md).

## 1. The clause that decides the game

The payoff table has one row people skip: **when a reviewer wrongfully rejects a fair claim, the
issuer is still paid** (and the reviewer pays `1.5a`). So a fair Charge is owed by *every*
opponent regardless of their Limits, while an Overcharge is paid only by the few who accept.
Measured on Game 62: **16 payers versus 3.**

The Charge is therefore **a cliff, not a slope**, and crossing `t` costs roughly 5× the income.
Game 62, Line Item 1, `t ∈ [8505, 10350)`: `error404 ai` charged 8,504.71, was paid by 16 of 16,
and collected **136,075 — 87 % of their entire Game**. We charged 10,349.89, were paid by 3, and
collected 31,050. They did not out-read the policy. They charged 22 % lower and landed on the
right side of a cliff.

## 2. The unlock: `t` is secret, but it is exactly recoverable

A settled Transaction *rejected while carrying a non-zero amount* is a wrongful rejection, which
proves `a ≤ t` and reveals the Charge; a rejection at zero proves `a > t`. Together they bracket
`t` for **every Line Item ever played**. `scripts/invert_fair_values.py --verify` reproduces every
published net to the cent across 52,224 settled rows.

That turns the whole tournament into a measurement instrument.
`scripts/replay_payoffs.py` scores any hypothetical submission against the real Field with all
sixteen opponents held fixed, and its self-check asserts that our *actual* submission reproduces
the authoritative net for every settled Game — a test, not a comment, because without it none of
our numbers mean anything. **Every claim in this write-up is a measurement rather than an
argument.** (Inference from the published leaderboard is permitted; we asked the organisers.)

## 3. The architecture, in one rule: the model reads, the engine prices

No model output is ever a price ([ADR 0001](docs/brainstorm/sebi/adr/0001-the-model-reads-the-engine-prices.md)).
Models emit **structured evidence** — a coverage probability with the policy clause quoted
verbatim, a price band, a quantity — and deterministic code turns evidence into a posterior over
`t` and the posterior into `(a, b)`:

```
blend      log m = Σ wᵢ·log mᵢ / Σ wᵢ,  wᵢ = 1/σᵢ²        (two model draws + Price Memory)
posterior  P(t) = (1−p)·δ(0) + p·LogNormal(log m, σ)      coverage is mass at zero, not a branch
Charge     a = k(σ)·m,   k = clamp(0.85 − 0.45·σ, 0.30, 0.80)     maximises k·P(t ≥ k·m)
Limit      b = Q⅓(P), then min(b, ceiling·m, a)           accept iff P(fair) > ⅔, so b is the ⅓ quantile
```

The `⅓` is derived, not tuned: rejecting a fair claim costs `1.5a`, rejecting a fraudulent one
costs nothing, so indifference sits at exactly two-thirds. Four separate attacks on it were
measured and lost.

The reason for the seam is auditability under repetition — this ran unattended 100 times, once
every 12.6 minutes, inside a 60-second window. **A prompt that emits a number cannot be swept,
folded or replayed; a prompt that emits evidence can.** It also means something is underneath when
the model goes away, and it did: **Games 82–89, eight consecutive triple-weighted Games, ran with
`model_draws=0`** because the endpoint returned 401 on every call. The blind floor posted at T+0,
Price Memory priced what it recognised, the fitted constants covered the rest, and those Games
banked **+254,092 weighted**. We did not notice until afterwards, which is the point.

## 4. The bar, and what cleared it

A change shipped only if it was positive on **all four folds** — odd Games, even Games, early
half, late half — never merely positive in total. The noise floor is measured, not assumed:
**26,622 over 18 Games** with an identical prompt, scaling as `√n`, so **±6,275 for a single
Game**. No single Game ever justified a change, however vivid it looked at 4 a.m.

Two changes moved real money, both on the Charge, both found by asking why a *specific* Line Item
lost. `BIG_ITEM_CHARGE_SCALE` 1.25 → 1.0: **+79,240** over 63 Games, with nine Line Items moving
from Overcharge to fair and none moving the other way. `CHARGE_TRUST_MEMORY = 1.15` — raise the
Charge only where a wording has been *watched settle*: **+80,613, four folds.** The control is
what makes it a channel effect rather than "charge more": doing the same to the model channel is
**−95,061 and 0/4**. Replayed over the last 10 Games, the pair moves us **−80,266 → +102,817**.

**11 of our 19 numbered hypotheses were measured and rejected**, each with the script that killed
it — a global Charge multiplier, the exact expected-income argmax, four attacks on the Limit,
copying the best rival's ratios (−280k to −380k), more ensemble draws (draw noise is 1.1 % of the
error). The sharpest one happened in the last hour: we shipped a coverage recalibration on a
genuine calibration table and a clean four-fold sweep, then **reverted it twenty minutes later**,
because checking the *mechanism* showed the model's coverage output is bimodal, so the correction
touched **4 Line Items in 573**. Its +5,057 was an incidental Limit nudge wearing a calibration
costume. A constant can be right about its data and wrong about its mechanism — and folds catch a
result driven by a few *Games*, never one driven by a few *items*.

---

# Why we think we succeeded — and where we did not

## Succeeded

- **We built a measurement instrument before we built a strategy.** Recovering `t` by inversion,
  then replaying counterfactuals against the real Field with all sixteen opponents fixed, meant
  every subsequent decision was settled by a number instead of an argument. Three claims we had
  written down as fact were falsified by it within a day.
- **We climbed from last to 5th.** After nine Games we were **17th of 17**. We are now **5th** on
  +231,298 weighted. Over the last twenty settled Games we are **2nd in the field by rate**
  (+6,897/Game); over the 69 Games since our estimator existed, **3rd of 17** at +5,254/Game —
  within **4.3 %** of the field leader.
- **The distribution is tight, which is the part we would actually defend.** **2 losing Games in
  the last 20, the worst costing 3,941**; 4 losing Games in the last 30, the fewest of any team.
  That is the **2nd-best risk-adjusted return in the field** (mean/σ = 0.72 vs 0.83). Five teams
  carry a single Game worse than −80,000; our deepest hole in thirty Games is −9,720. In an
  insurance book, the narrow distribution is the number that matters.
- **The architecture degraded instead of failing.** Eight triple-weighted Games ran with the model
  channel completely dark and still banked +254,092, because no scored number ever depended on a
  model being reachable.
- **We priced uptime correctly.** Break-even uptime is 71 %; rescuing a Game is worth `93t` and
  improving one `37t`, so **showing up is 2.5× being right**. A blind floor posts plausible numbers
  at T+0 before the Case is decrypted, submissions merge per Line Item so partial output is never
  discarded, and a supervisor restarts the runner on any crash. R10 was confirmed against a real
  opponent: `makalu` went dark, paid us **179,992.64** across the season, and collected **0.00**
  from anyone.

## Did not succeed

- **We spent the first quarter of the tournament building the instrument instead of scoring.**
  Games 1–25 cost **−322,595**, which is larger than our entire current season net. Every point of
  our deficit is there. The rate says the decision was right; the total says we paid full price
  for it.
- **The estimate, not the strategy, is the entire remaining gap — and we found that out late.**
  `a = b = t` reaches **100.3 %** of the best possible play and is within 3 % on 70 of 70 Games,
  while `a = b = t̂` scores **−50,140**. The **2,498,118** between them is pure estimation error.
  We optimised the decision rules to their measured argmax and it barely mattered; the best
  constant available anywhere in a full sweep moves the total by ~18k. Arguably we spent our
  effort one layer too low.
- **We diagnosed our largest open lever and deliberately did not ship it.** Policy clause 7.1.5
  has two halves — indemnity is confined to the affected parts, *but* "where an affected room was
  wetted as a whole, the whole of that room is treated as affected". The model reads only the
  first half. Game 74 returned coverage of 0.01–0.05 on 20 of 31 Line Items for **€41,710, 87 % of
  that Game's penalties**. Perfect coverage is worth **+1,173/Game**. It is a prompt change, it
  could not be validated without spending the live runner's quota, and it would have landed six
  Games before the 3× window with no way to tell a fix from a regression. We think the call was
  right and the outcome is still a loss.
- **Eight triple-weighted Games ran with the model dark and we did not notice.** It is the best
  evidence we have that the fallback architecture works, and it is also an operational failure: we
  had no alert on `model_draws=0`, during the most valuable Games of the tournament.
- **We were beaten on the thing we understood best.** We wrote down that the Charge is a cliff and
  we still sat above `t` too often; `error404 ai` took 136,075 off a single Line Item by charging
  22 % lower than us. Knowing the mechanism and calibrating to it are different achievements, and
  we only closed the gap at Game 63.

---

**No claim data is checked into this repository.** Not the Cases, not the invoices, not the
policies — and not the four derived paths that would reproduce them (raw model replies, per-Game
reviews, the decision log and the settled lessons all carry policy wording or invoice Line Item
text). They generate locally and are ignored. Short single-clause quotations appear where the
argument needs them, as citation rather than as an archive.

input.prompt:
Working dir: `/Users/sebastianrogg/PycharmProjects/Hackathons & Projekte/WireClaim`

URGENT — hard deadline in ~45 minutes. Produce publication-quality charts for a hackathon pitch deck and a LaTeX paper. Team name is **"Bin busy"**.

## What exists
`case_analysis/` already computes everything. **Read `case_analysis/balance.py` and `case_analysis/DATA_LAYOUT.md` first**, and reuse its data loading. Key data already on disk:
- `case_analysis/data/balance.csv` — cumulative balance per team per game, columns: `game` + one column per team (94 rows). This is the master series.
- `case_analysis/data/binbusy_money.csv` — our per-game `income, expenses_accepted, lawyer_count, lawyer_total, expenses, net`
- `case_analysis/data/teams.csv`, `tvalues.csv`, `table_averages.csv`

`case_analysis/data/balance.png` is the existing chart. It works but is **far too cluttered for a projected slide** — 17 labelled lines, a legend covering the plot, unreadable x tick labels.

**Find the Python that has matplotlib** — it is NOT the pixi env. The PNGs were regenerated at 10:50 today, so try `python3`, `/usr/local/bin/python3`, `uv run`, a venv in the repo, or `python3 -m pip install --user matplotlib` as a last resort. Report which interpreter you used.

## Verified facts to annotate with (do NOT recompute, do NOT contradict)
- 94 of 100 games settled. We are currently **5th of 17**, +231,298 weighted / **+39,936 unweighted**.
- **Rank trajectory: 17th of 17 (DEAD LAST) at Games 9–12**; 16th at 13–18; 15th at 8 and 19–34; 12th at G40; 7th at G50–60; **5th permanently from Game 76**.
- **Games 1–25: −322,595** total (−12,904/game) — before the current estimator existed. This is the whole deficit.
- **Games 26–94: +362,531** (+5,254/game) — 3rd of 17 by rate in that window.
- **Games 75–94: +137,942** (+6,897/game) — **2nd of 17 by rate**. Leader Codacabana +12,253.
- **Games 81–100 are weighted 3×.** 81–94 played so far.
- **Games 82–89: the model channel was dark** (endpoint 401'd, model_draws=0) and we still banked +254,092 weighted.
- Charge fixes went live around **Game 63–66**.
- Consistency (Games 75–94, unweighted): our σ = 9,639, mean 6,897, **mean/σ = 0.716 → 2nd best in field** (Codacabana 0.825). **Only 2 losing games in 20; worst −3,941.** Over 30 games: 4 losing games — fewest of any team. Five teams have single games worse than −80,000.

## Deliverables — write PNG **and** PDF (vector) of each, into `presentation/figures/`
Produce **two colour variants of each**: `*-dark.png/pdf` for the slide deck (background `#0B0C0E`, text `#E7E5E4`, muted `#6B6763`, single accent `#E8B84B`) and `*-light.pdf` for the LaTeX paper (white bg, black text, one accent). Save the generating script as `case_analysis/pitch_figures.py` so it is reproducible.

**FIG 1 — `balance-annotated`** (the hero chart). Cumulative balance, all 94 games.
- All 16 rival teams as thin, low-opacity grey lines, NO per-line labels, NO legend for them.
- **"Bin busy" as one thick accent-coloured line** that dominates. Label it at the right end.
- Label ONLY the current top-3 rivals faintly at their right end, for scale.
- **Shade and label the eras** as background bands with text: `G1–25 no estimator (−322,595)`, `G26–62 estimator + learning loop`, `G63–80 Charge fixes live`, `G81–100 3× weighted`. Add a slim marker band for `G82–89 model channel dark`.
- Annotate two points on our line with a leader line: **"17th of 17"** near G9 and **"5th"** at the right end.
- Clean x axis: ticks every 10 games, readable. Y axis in thousands with a € or k suffix, horizontal gridlines only, no top/right spines.
- Title should state the claim, e.g. "Last place to 5th — cumulative net, 94 settled Games".

**FIG 2 — `consistency`** — the "we are unusually stable" chart. Pick the clearest of these and justify your pick in one line:
   (a) scatter of mean per-game net (x) vs σ (y) for all 17 teams over G75–94, our point highlighted and labelled, with an iso-ratio line; or
   (b) horizontal bar / dot plot of mean÷σ ranked, ours highlighted; or
   (c) per-game net distribution: our worst-game vs each team's worst-game, ranked.
   Whichever you choose it must make **"2nd best risk-adjusted return, only 2 losing games in 20, worst −3,941"** visually obvious at 4 metres.

**FIG 3 — `per-game-net`** — our own per-game net as a bar chart across all 94 games (green above zero, red below), with the same era bands as FIG 1 and a rolling-10 mean line on top. This shows the variance collapsing after the estimator ships.

## Quality bar
- Must be legible **projected at 4 metres**: minimum effective font ~11pt at final size, thick lines, no thin grey-on-grey.
- Figure size ~16:9 for FIG 1 and FIG 3 (e.g. 16×9 in at 200 dpi), FIG 2 can be squarer.
- No chartjunk: no 3D, no shadows, no rainbow. One accent colour carries meaning.
- `matplotlib` only. No seaborn styling that overrides the palette.
- **Every number you print on a chart must come from the data or the verified list above.** Do not invent.

When done, report: which interpreter you used, the exact files written, your FIG 2 choice + why, and ANY number in the verified list that the underlying CSV contradicts. Do not modify anything outside `presentation/figures/` and `case_analysis/pitch_figures.py`.

# WireClaim — the exact formula chain, stage by stage

Source of truth: working tree at `4bf4af5` (2026-08-23). Every constant below was read out of the file named; the worked examples were produced by **importing and executing `src/pricing/engine.py`**, not by hand.

## A. The formula chain

### Stage 0 — T+0 s: blind floor, before anything is known
`blind_floor()` — `main.py:128–156`, called at `main.py:176` **before** `load_case` at `main.py:184`.

```

```

| name | value | file:line |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `BLIND_LINE_ITEMS` | `40` | `main.py:125` |
| `STANDARD_CHARGE` | `300.0` | `src/strategies/fast_path.py:40` |
| `STANDARD_LIMIT` | `35.0` | `src/strategies/fast_path.py:41` |
| `RUN_SECONDS` | `60.0` | `main.py:27` |

Wire format `PUT /api/games/{id}/submissions`, body `{"index","charge_price","acceptance_limit"}` (`src/api/tournament.py:185–207`). Upsert, last write wins. Only clamp on the wire is finite + non-negative (`_validate_price`, `tournament.py:83–92`).

### Stage 1 — T+0 to ~T+3 s: key, extract, parse
`GET /api/games/{id}/key` polled **every 0.5 s** while `403` (`src/data/case_loader.py:56–72`, sleep line 71) → `7z x` (`:82–91`) → invoice parse. Index is the **printed POS number, gaps preserved**; a dash-only quantity/unit row sets `quantity_missing=True` (`case_loader.py:17–46`). On failure, `main.py:185` logs "blind floor stands" and Stage 0's numbers are the Game.

### Stage 2 — `CaseData` exists: deterministic baseline
`standard_values` (`fast_path.py:63–83`) → `(300.00, 35.00)` on the real index set, published at `main.py:207` with `reason="case_loaded"`. `RunManager.__init__` refuses an empty standard Proposal (`main.py:49–50`) — the mechanical guarantee no index is ever unpriced.

### Stage 3 — evidence, four channels
`Evidence(index, coverage_probability=0.9, price_low=0, price_median=0, price_high=0)` — `engine.py:960–990`.

**Channel A — dash quantity ⇒ worthless.** `channels.py:71–85`, dispatched `:171–173`:
```
coverage = 0.0,  band = (SETTLED_MEDIAN*0.5, SETTLED_MEDIAN, SETTLED_MEDIAN*2) = (48.5, 97.0, 194.0)
```
Band deliberately non-zero: `t = 0` ⇒ a rejected Charge is free (R6c). `price_item` also gets `confirmed_uncovered=True` (`strategy.py:157`).

**Channel B — Price Memory.** `channels.py:144–198`, band built in `memory.py:337–392`:
```
values = every stored observation restated as a GROSS total for this quantity
median = statistics.median(values)
low    = min(values[0],  median*exp(-0.43))
high   = max(values[-1], median*exp(+0.43))
```
The widening matters: raw spread contained true `t` on only **42 %** of leave-one-out hits; widened, **65 %** (`memory.py:202–206`). Per-unit rule at `memory.py:394–459` moved RMSLE **0.493 → 0.442** overall, **0.993 → 0.660** on mixed-basis entries. Coverage is fixed at `_MEMORY_COVERAGE = 0.9` (`channels.py:55`) — memory never carries a coverage verdict (6 of 15 repeated wordings flip between `t = 0` and `t > 0`).

**Channel C — the model, two framings concurrently.** `model.request_evidence` (`model.py:145–181`), one whole-Case call per framing against a Policy sliced to Parts `{3,4,5,7,11}` (`slice.py:33`), failing open below `MIN_SLICE_CHARS = 2000` (`slice.py:40, :107`). `ENSEMBLE_PROMPTS = (PROMPT, PROMPT_UNANCHORED)` (`prompts.py:93`). Parser reads **only** coverage + three prices, and **sorts** the band (`model.py:80–82`); coverage clamped `≤ 1.0` (`:85`).

Draw budget — `strategy.py:194–198`, `:206–214`:
```
timeout     = max( min(55.0, deadline − now − 5.0), 1.0 )
outer guard = timeout + 0.5
```
`LLM_TIMEOUT_SECONDS = 55.0` (`constants.py:31`), `SUBMISSION_RESERVE_SECONDS = 5.0` (`:40`), `DRAW_GRACE_SECONDS = 0.5` (`:53`). Both draws under `asyncio.gather` (`strategy.py:224`); a dead draw returns `{}` (`:215–221`).

**Channel D — aggregate sub-limit discount.** `channels.py:88–141`. **Runs at `strategy.py:134`, i.e. BEFORE `combine`, not after.** Where ≥2 "valuables" members both carry model evidence, all but the dearest get `coverage := min(coverage, 0.30)` (`_AGGREGATE_DISCOUNT_COVERAGE`, `channels.py:45`) — below `COVERAGE_FLOOR`, so the Limit collapses with no second special case. Worth **+2,026.89** over Game 44, no-op elsewhere.

### Stage 4 — `blend`: the two ensemble draws (log space, widen on disagreement)
`blend.py:51–83`, per index:
```
mean_log = (1/n)·Σ log(median_i)                                  # :68
asserted = (1/n)·Σ σ_i,  σ_i = sigma_of(draw_i)                   # :69
observed = sqrt( (1/n)·Σ (log median_i − mean_log)² )             # :70  (population sd)
σ_blend  = sqrt(asserted² + observed²)                            # :72
median   = exp(mean_log)
(low,median,high) = ( median·exp(−1.645·σ_blend), median, median·exp(+1.645·σ_blend) )
coverage = mean over EVERY draw that spoke, including ones that priced 0   # :78
```
`sigma_of` (`:44–48`): `log(high/low)/(2·1.645)`, else `MODEL_SIGMA_PRIOR = 0.6`. One usable draw returns unchanged (`:56–57`); all-zero keeps the verdict rather than inventing a band (`:62–65`).
Measured: one draw **+51,712**, two **+80,229** (G1–15, 17–19); two draws beat one by **+28,625** (`prompts.py:90–92`).

### Stage 5 — `combine`: the inverse-variance blend
`blend.py:86–138`:
```
w_model  = 1/0.6²  = 2.777777777777778     # :123
w_memory = 1/0.43² = 5.408328826392645     # :124
W        =           8.186106604170423     # :125
median   = exp( (w_model·log m_model + w_memory·log m_memory) / W )   # :126–129
σ_comb   = sqrt(1/W)                                                  # :130
coverage = model.coverage_probability   # memory NEVER supplies coverage  # :134
```
**Exact normalised weights: model 0.33932831712240774, memory 0.6606716828775923** — so `median = m_model^0.339328 × m_memory^0.660672`.

**σ_comb = 0.3495113648568052, a CONSTANT.** This is the most missable fact in the chain: `combine` uses the *prior* 0.6, not `sigma_of(model)`. So on **every** memory-backed item the posterior width is fixed and **Stage 4's carefully-widened ensemble σ is thrown away** (its median survives, its width does not).

Four branches in test order: `model is None` → memory; `memory` unusable → model; **`model.price_median <= 0`** → keep model's coverage, take memory's band (**+3,190**, positive in all four Games it touches — previously these dropped onto `FALLBACK_MEDIAN` and were all Charged 39.62); `memory.coverage == 0` → coverage stays 0, take model's band.

### Stage 6 — `price_item`, the only place a scored number is decided
`engine.py:1060–1188`.

**6.0 Repair** (`with_defaults`, `:973–990`): no positive value ⇒ `(30.0, 60.0, 120.0)`; missing low ⇒ `median·0.5`; missing high ⇒ `median·2`; coverage clamped to `[0,1]`.

**6.1 Posterior**
```
posterior(t) = (1 − p) · δ(0) + p · Lognormal(median = t̂, σ)
implied_sigma(low,median,high) = min( log(high/low) / (2·1.645), 2.0 )    # :1001–1011, 1.0 on a broken band

**6.2 The Charge** (`:1087–1097`)
```
k = clamp(0.85 − 0.45·σ, 0.30, 0.80)
a = k · median
if memory_backed:                 a *= 1.15      # CHARGE_TRUST_MEMORY
if median >= 1000.0:              a *= 1.0       # BIG_ITEM_CHARGE_SCALE — a no-op since Game 63

**The Charge never reads coverage** (`:1084–1086`) — deliberate and free.

```

else:
    conditional = (1/3 − (1 − covered)) / covered
    ceiling     = 1.00 if memory_backed else 0.45

**6.5 Worked examples (executed)** — memory-backed, coverage 0.9, σ = 0.3495113648568052:

| ---: | --- | ---: | ---: |
| 100 | 56.27–177.70 | **79.66** | **79.80** ← `b > a` |

p='writeup.tex'; s=open(p).read()
add = r'''
% --- the hero figure, included only once the chart script has run -------------
\IfFileExists{figures/balance-annotated-light.pdf}{%
\begin{figure*}[t]
\centering
\includegraphics[width=\textwidth]{figures/balance-annotated-light.pdf}
\caption{Cumulative net over 94 settled Games, all 17 teams. We are the heavy line. The deficit is
Games 1--25, before the estimator existed; the slope after Game~26 is the method. Games 82--89 ran
with the model channel returning 401 on every call.}
\end{figure*}}{}

\onecolumn
\section*{\textcolor{accent}{Why we think we succeeded --- and where we did not}}
\vspace{-0.4em}
\begin{multicols}{2}
\subsection*{Succeeded}
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{We built the measuring instrument before the strategy.} Equation~\eqref{eq:inversion}
recovers $\fair$ exactly, so every later decision was settled by replaying it against the real
Field rather than argued. Three claims we had written down as fact were falsified within a day.
\item \textbf{Last place to 5\textsuperscript{th}.} 17\textsuperscript{th} of 17 after nine Games;
5\textsuperscript{th} from Game~76. Second in the field by rate over the last twenty Games; third
of seventeen over the 69 Games since the estimator existed, within $4.3\%$ of the leader.
\item \textbf{The distribution is tight, and that is the result we would defend.} Two losing Games
in the last twenty, the worst costing $3{,}941$; four in the last thirty, fewest of any team.
Mean-to-$\sigma$ of $0.72$, second best in the field, while five teams carry single Games worse
than $-80{,}000$. In an insurance book the narrow distribution is the number that matters.
\item \textbf{It degraded instead of failing.} Eight consecutive $3\times$-weighted Games ran with
the model channel completely dark and still banked $+254{,}092$, because no scored number ever
depended on a model being reachable.
\item \textbf{We priced uptime correctly.} Break-even uptime is $71\%$; rescuing a Game is worth
$93\fair$ against $37\fair$ for improving one, so \emph{showing up is 2.5$\times$ being right}. A
blind floor posts at T$+$0 before the Case is decrypted, submissions merge per Line Item, and a
supervisor restarts on any crash. Confirmed against a real opponent: \texttt{makalu} went dark,
paid us $179{,}993$ across the season and collected $0.00$ from anyone.
\end{itemize}

\subsection*{Did not succeed}
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{We spent the first quarter of the tournament building the instrument instead of
scoring.} Games 1--25 cost $-322{,}595$ --- more than our entire current season net. The rate says
the decision was right; the total says we paid full price for it.
\item \textbf{The estimate, not the strategy, is the whole remaining gap --- and we learned that
late.} $\charge=\limitv=\fair$ reaches $100.3\%$ of optimal play; $\charge=\limitv=\est$ scores
$-50{,}140$. The $2{,}498{,}118$ between them is pure estimation error. We tuned decision rules to
their measured argmax and it barely mattered; arguably we worked one layer too low.
\item \textbf{We diagnosed our largest open lever and deliberately did not ship it.} Policy clause
7.1.5 has two halves and the model reads only the first. Game~74 returned coverage $0.01$--$0.05$
on 20 of 31 Line Items, for $87\%$ of that Game's penalties. Perfect coverage is worth
$+1{,}173$/Game. It is a prompt change that could not be validated without spending the live
runner's quota, six Games before the $3\times$ window. We think the call was right and the outcome
is still a loss.
\item \textbf{Eight triple-weighted Games ran with the model dark and we did not notice.} It is the
best evidence we have that the architecture works, and simultaneously an operational failure: no
alert on \texttt{model\_draws=0}, during the most valuable Games of the tournament.
\item \textbf{We were beaten on the thing we understood best.} We had written down that the Charge
is a cliff and still sat above $\fair$ too often; a rival took $136{,}075$ off a single Line Item
by charging $22\%$ lower than us. Knowing a mechanism and being calibrated to it are different
achievements, and we only closed that gap at Game~63.
\end{itemize}
\end{multicols}

\vspace{0.6em}
\noindent\rule{\linewidth}{0.4pt}\\[0.3em]
{\footnotesize\textbf{No claim data is checked into this repository} --- not the Cases, the invoice
PDFs or the policies, and not the four derived paths that would reproduce them (raw model replies,
per-Game reviews, the submission-time decision log and the settled lessons all carry policy wording
or invoice Line Item text). All four regenerate locally and are git-ignored. Single-clause
quotations appear where the argument needs them, as citation rather than as an archive.
Every figure in this document is reproducible from a script in the repository.\par}

'''

open(p,'w').write(s); print('ok')

## The spine

One idea, and everything hangs off it: **the hidden fair value `t` is exactly recoverable after
settlement.** That turns a hidden-information game into a measurement problem. The cliff is what
the recovered `t` *revealed*; the twelve dead hypotheses are what the replay harness *killed*;
"the model reads, the engine prices" is the architecture that *made replay possible*.

## Timing — 5:00

| min | slides | what you actually say |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 0:00–0:40 | title, 01, 02 | The game in two sentences. | 0:40–1:30 | 03, 04 | **The unlock.** A rejection carrying money proves `a ≤ t`; a rejection at zero proves `a > t`. That brackets `t` for every Line Item ever played — 52,224 rows, every published net reproduced to the cent. So we can replay any hypothetical submission against the real Field with all sixteen opponents held fixed. *Every number in this pitch is a measurement, not an argument.* |
| 1:30–2:20 | 05, 06 | **The architecture.** No model output is ever a price — models emit evidence (coverage probability + the clause quoted verbatim + a price band), deterministic code prices it. A prompt that emits a number can't be swept or replayed; one that emits evidence can. And it degrades: Games 82–89, eight triple-weighted Games, the model 401'd on every call — **+254,092 anyway.** Then the four lines of arithmetic. Point at the ⅓: *derived, not tuned.* |
| 2:20–2:50 | 07 | **60 seconds, 100 times, unattended, half of it overnight.** Blind floor at T+0 before we even have the key. Break-even uptime is 71 % — showing up is 2.5× being right. |

Then: **12 of 20 hypotheses killed**, one of them **reverted 20 minutes after it shipped** because the mechanism check showed it touched 4 items in 573. |

No, and we asked. The published Transactions are settled results; inference from them is not
obtaining secret thresholds. The organisers confirmed it. We never touched another team's key or
an unsettled submission.

**"You're 5th. Why should we care?"**

−322,595 with no estimator; over the last twenty we are 2nd in the field by rate. We are not
claiming that wins — we are telling you which number is which.

Everything's committed. Here's where it stands with ~25 minutes to the pitch.

## Do this now

**Export the deck to PDF and upload it to ehl.gg.** The kick-off deck says *"only use slides submitted on ehl.gg"*, and you can't edit after upload. Open `presentation/index.html` in Chrome → Print → Save as PDF → **Landscape, margins None, Background graphics ON**.

| file | what |
|---|---|
| `WRITEUP.md` | the judged write-up at root, where Hailong said to put it |
| `presentation/writeup.pdf` | 4-page LaTeX paper with the derivations + balance figure ([source](presentation/writeup.tex)) |

| `presentation/RUNSHEET.md` | per-slide timing, what to cut, and the 3 questions you'll get |

The deck follows the judges' own rubric (kick-off p21): **solution → demo → proof**. Spine is the t-inversion, because everything else is downstream of it.

## Three wrong numbers were in the docs you were about to be judged on

The one that matters: **`METHODOLOGY.md` claimed "+17,302 per Game" as our rate.** That's *eyay's five-Game total* for Games 21–25, transcribed out of `strategy2-games.md:308` into a sentence about us. Real figure: **+6,897** — still 2nd in the field, but off by 2.5× and attributed to the wrong team. Also fixed: "11 of 19 hypotheses" (the ledger has 20 labels and 12 rejections), and `methodology-full.md` still described the `b ≤ a` clamp as live when it was released at Game 66.

## Two things read *better* than you thought

- **The climb is bigger.** Not second-to-last — you were **17th of 17, dead last, at Games 9–12**. At Game 23 you were 15th. "Last place to 5th" is both accurate and stronger.
- **"Five teams worse than −80,000" is seven.** You were understating your own consistency case.

On Strategy 2: you said ~Game 20, and CLAUDE.md records Games 21–24 still submitting `STANDARD_LIMIT` of 35 on every Line Item. So I wrote "before the estimator was **working**" rather than "existed" — true to both, and it keeps the measured G1–25 era boundary intact.

- **`docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` §4 is materially stale in ~10 places** (says `LIMIT_CEILING_MEMORY = 0.75`, asserts "`b ≤ a` always holds", wrong reserve seconds, wrong channel ordering). No judge will read it before 12:30, but it'll mislead whoever picks this up next.

body = r'''\section{The game, and the row everybody skips}

Per ordered pair (issuer $H$, reviewer $I$) and Line Item, with hidden fair value $\fair$ and
hidden cap $c\ge\max(4\fair,2000)$, the reviewer's payoff is
\begin{equation}
\pi_I=
\begin{cases}
-\charge & \charge\le\fair,\ \charge\le\limitv\\
\mathbf{-1.5\,\charge} & \charge\le\fair,\ \charge>\limitv\\
-\min(\charge,c) & \charge>\fair,\ \charge\le\limitv\\
0 & \charge>\fair,\ \charge>\limitv
\end{cases}
\label{eq:reviewer}
\end{equation}
while the issuer receives $\charge$ whenever $\charge\le\fair$ --- \emph{whatever the reviewer
does} --- and $\min(\charge,c)$ only if an Overcharge is accepted. So a fair Charge is owed by all
$N=16$ opponents; an Overcharge is paid by the few whose Limit happens to admit it. Measured on
Game~62: \textbf{16 payers versus 3}. The Charge is a \textbf{cliff, not a slope}: one rival
charged $22\%$ less than us on a single Line Item, was paid by $16/16$, and took $136{,}075$ ---
$87\%$ of their whole Game.

\section{Both decisions fall out of \eqref{eq:reviewer}}

\textbf{The Charge.} With $F$ the posterior CDF of $\fair$ and $q$ the fraction of opponents whose
Limit admits $\charge$, income per opponent is $\charge[\,1-F(\charge)+F(\charge)q(\charge)]$.
Empirically $q$ collapses across $\charge=\fair$ ($16/16$ below, $17\%$ at $1.0$--$1.3\times$,
$7\%$ above), and a \emph{mis-measured} $q$ costs more than assuming $q=0$, so we maximise the
conservative objective. For $\fair\sim\mathrm{LogN}(\ln m,\sigma^2)$ and $\charge=k\,m$,
\begin{equation}
R(k)\;\propto\;k\,\Phi\!\left(-\tfrac{\ln k}{\sigma}\right),
\qquad \charge=k(\sigma)\,m,
\end{equation}
whose maximiser is \emph{strictly below 1 at every precision} and falls as the estimate degrades
($0.70$ at $\sigma{=}0.25$, $0.60$ at $0.45$, $0.45$ at $0.75$). We ship
$k(\sigma)=\mathrm{clamp}(0.85-0.45\sigma,\,0.30,\,0.80)$.

\textbf{The Limit.} By \eqref{eq:reviewer} accepting costs $\charge$; rejecting costs
$1.5\charge$ \emph{only if the claim was fair}. Accepting is therefore right exactly when
$\charge<1.5\charge\,P(\fair\ge\charge)$, i.e.\ $P(\text{fair})>\frac23$, so the Limit is the
\textbf{one-third quantile of the posterior} --- derived, not tuned. Coverage needs no branch:
with $p=P(\text{covered})$ the posterior is a spike-and-slab,
\begin{equation}
P(\fair)=(1-p)\,\delta_0+p\,\mathrm{LogN}(\ln m,\sigma^2),
\end{equation}
so when $p\le\frac23$ the bottom third \emph{is} the atom at zero and $\limitv=0$ emerges on its
own. $40\%$ of settled Line Items have $\fair=0$, and paying on one is a pure loss.

\section{The model reads; the engine prices}

No model output is ever a price. Models emit \emph{structured evidence} --- a coverage probability
with the policy clause quoted verbatim, a price band, a quantity --- and deterministic code turns
evidence into the posterior and the posterior into $(\charge,\limitv)$. Channels combine by
inverse-variance weighting in log space, $\hat\mu=\sum w_i\mu_i/\sum w_i$ with $w_i=\sigma_i^{-2}$,
at $\sigma_{\text{memory}}=0.43$ against $\sigma_{\text{model}}=0.60$.

The reason is auditability under repetition: this ran unattended 100 times, once every 12.6
minutes, in a 60-second window. \textbf{A prompt that emits a number cannot be swept, folded or
replayed; a prompt that emits evidence can.} It also degrades rather than fails --- \textbf{Games
82--89, eight consecutive $3\times$-weighted Games, ran with the model endpoint returning 401 on
every call} and still banked $+254{,}092$.

\section{Why our counterfactuals are measurements}

The published transaction log inverts. A \emph{rejected} transaction carrying a non-zero amount was
a wrongful rejection, which by row~2 of \eqref{eq:reviewer} occurs only when the Charge was fair; a
rejection at zero occurs only when it was not. Hence
\begin{equation}
\boxed{\;\fair\in\Big[\max_{\text{rej},\,\text{amt}>0}\charge_\alpha,\;\;
\min_{\text{rej},\,\text{amt}=0}\charge_\alpha\Big)\;}
\label{eq:inversion}
\end{equation}
brackets $\fair$ for \emph{every Line Item ever played}. Over 52{,}224 settled rows the
reconstruction reproduces every published net \textbf{to the cent}, so we can replay any
hypothetical submission against the real Field with all sixteen opponents held fixed. The replay's
self-check asserts that our \emph{actual} submission reproduces the authoritative net for every
settled Game --- a test, not a comment.

\textbf{The bar.} Positive on \textbf{all four folds} (odd, even, early, late), never merely in
total, against a \emph{measured} noise floor of $26{,}622$ over 18 Games --- $\pm6{,}275$ for one
Game, which is why no single Game ever justified a change. Of twenty numbered hypotheses,
\textbf{twelve were measured and rejected}. One shipped and was \textbf{reverted twenty minutes
later}: it passed a real calibration table and all four folds, but a mechanism check showed the
model's coverage output is bimodal, so it moved \textbf{4 Line Items in 573}. A constant can be
right about its data and wrong about its mechanism.

\begin{tabular}{lrrr}
\toprule
window & total & per Game & rate rank\\

G1--25 \emph{(estimator not working)} & \textcolor{bad}{$-322{,}595$} & $-12{,}904$ & ---\\

season, weighted & \textcolor{good}{$+231{,}298$} & --- & \textbf{5 / 17}\\

Done and committed — with two minutes to spare.

## For submission

**`presentation/writeup.pdf` — exactly 2 pages**, which is what Hailong asked for:
- **p1** — the approach with the derivations (the cliff, why `a = k(σ)·m` sits below the estimate, why the Limit is the ⅓ quantile, and the boxed `t`-inversion)
- **p2** — the balance chart + succeeded / did-not-succeed bullets in two columns, and the no-claim-data statement

**`presentation/writeup-full.pdf` — 4 pages** for anyone who wants the strategy. It carries what the two-pager had no room for: the `b ≤ a` clamp we removed at Game 66 and what Game 65 item 3 cost to find it, six of the twelve rejected hypotheses with euro figures, and the two traps (conditioning on the outcome, censoring).

`WRITEUP.md` stays at root for browser reading; README now points at the PDF first.

## For the pitch (now)

`presentation/index.html` — 10 slides, timed to 5:00 in `RUNSHEET.md`. `appendix.html` has the full 20 for Q&A.

## Still running

The **rebased-at-Game-20 chart** you asked for — everyone indexed to 0 at G20, cumulative from there. I also had it compute the honest numbers: our rank on that rebased measure, and a **sensitivity check rebasing at Game 26** instead, since Games 21–24 still submitted the fallback Limit of 35 and G20 is arguably generous to us. I'll report both when it lands — if the rank differs between the two cuts, you'll want to know before quoting it on stage.

One flag: I corrected "since the estimator existed" to "was working" in the bullets, but **the chart's own era band still reads "G1–25 no estimator"**. It's baked into the PNG and I couldn't re-render it before the deadline without risking the file you're presenting from. If anyone asks, the honest line is: Strategy 2 went live around Game 20, but Games 21–24 still submitted the fallback Limit, so it wasn't really working until Game 26.

input.command:

\section{What we would fix next, and why it is all one thing}

Both numbers we submit are functions of the \emph{same} estimate. $\charge=k(\sigma)\,\est$ and
$\limitv=Q_{1/3}$ of a posterior centred on $\est$. So a single estimation error is paid
\textbf{twice, in opposite directions}, and this is the whole of our remaining gap:

\begin{itemize}
\item $\est$ \textbf{too low} $\Rightarrow$ $\limitv$ too low $\Rightarrow$ we wrongfully reject a
\emph{fair} claim $\Rightarrow$ we pay $\mathbf{1.5\charge}$. The half-charge goes to nobody. This
is the largest single line in our costs, and note it fires \emph{only} on claims that were fair ---
rejecting a genuine Overcharge is free.
\item $\est$ \textbf{too high} $\Rightarrow$ $\charge>\fair$ $\Rightarrow$ thirteen of sixteen
opponents refuse it $\Rightarrow$ we earn \textbf{nothing} on an item we were owed money for.
Crossing $\fair$ costs roughly $5\times$ the income.
\end{itemize}

\noindent
That is why $\charge=\limitv=\fair$ reaches $100.3\%$ of optimal play while
$\charge=\limitv=\est$ scores $-50{,}140$: the $2{,}498{,}118$ between them is not strategy, and no
decision rule reaches it. In priority order, what we would build with more time:

\begin{enumerate}
\item \textbf{Calibrate the band --- worth more than any constant in the engine.} The model asserts
a median $\sigma$ of $0.375$ against a realised RMSLE near $0.80$: overconfident by $2.1\times$.
Worse, the width carries \emph{no signal} --- split items by band width and the narrow third scores
RMSLE $0.847$ against the wide third's $0.733$, i.e.\ slightly \emph{backwards}. So $k(\sigma)$
multiplies a number that does not measure what it claims to. The line is right; its input is not.
\item \textbf{Fix the coverage read.} Policy clause 7.1.5 confines indemnity to the affected parts,
\emph{but} adds that where a room was wetted as a whole, the whole room is treated as affected. The
model reads the first half only. Game~74 returned coverage $0.01$--$0.05$ on 20 of 31 Line Items,
$87\%$ of that Game's penalties. Perfect coverage is worth $+1{,}173$/Game on all four folds.
\item \textbf{Separate the genuinely large items from the phantoms.} Of 23 items we believed worth
over $2{,}000$, \textbf{14 were worth under half that}. An observable that splits the 9 real ones
would let us charge confidently where it is safe --- today we cannot, so we charge low everywhere.
\item \textbf{Widen the memory channel.} A wording we have watched settle has a measured log error
of $\mathbf{0.43}$ against the model's realised $1.66$--$2.20$, but memory only reaches about
$22\%$ of Line Items. Every point of coverage there is a direct reduction in $\sigma$ --- and by
the first item above, $\sigma$ is what sets both numbers.
\end{enumerate}
TEXEOF

Committed. Here's where things stand while the data refresh runs.

## Clock correction

It's **11:24**, not the ~12:40 I'd been assuming — I'd been over-counting elapsed time. You have ~35 min to the 12:00 submission and ~65 to the pitch.

## What I added on "where we'd improve"

Your description pointed at something worth stating as one mechanism rather than three complaints. Both numbers come from the **same** `t̂` — `a = k(σ)·t̂`, and `b` is a quantile of a posterior centred on `t̂`. So one estimation error gets paid **twice, in opposite directions**:

- `t̂` **too low** → `b` too low → you wrongfully reject a **fair** claim → you pay `1.5a`. That's your lawyer, and it only ever fires on claims that were fair — rejecting a genuine Overcharge is free.
- `t̂` **too high** → `a` crosses `t` → 13 of 16 refuse → you earn **nothing** on an item you were owed for.

That's exactly your "b too low → lawyer → then a too high", and framing it as one error paid on both sides is stronger than listing them, because it explains why `a=b=t` is 100.3% of optimal while `a=b=t̂` is −50,140.

Ordered fixes: **calibrate the band first** (asserted σ 0.375 vs realised 0.80 — and the width doesn't even *order* the error, so `k(σ)` multiplies a number that measures nothing), then coverage (+1,173/Game), then splitting the 9 real large items from the 14 phantoms, then widening Price Memory past the 22% of items it reaches.

Landed in: new **slide 09** in both decks, a section in `writeup-full.pdf`, a sharpened bullet in the 2-pager (still exactly 2 pages), `WRITEUP.md`, and a written-out Q&A answer in `RUNSHEET.md`.

## Still running

The refresh to **97 Games**. I asked it to re-verify every consistency claim you listed, and to flag loudly if any superlative broke — specifically "2 losing Games in 20", "worst −3,941", "mean/σ 0.72, 2nd in field", "4 in 30, fewest of any team", and the rebased "2nd of 17". content.text:
Done — `writeup.pdf` page 2 now leads with the indexed-at-Game-20 chart, at a size that actually reads in print.

**Why this is the right call:** a judge reading two pages sees *one* figure, and the rebase is the one that answers "are these people any good." Season total says 5th; zeroing everyone at Game 20 says **2nd of 17**. The entire difference between those two numbers is Games 1–19.

**One thing I kept in, deliberately:** the caption still states the conservative anchor — *"At the Game 26 anchor we are 3rd, top three inside 9,702."* You're choosing the flattering cut, and saying so in the caption is what stops it reading as a cherry-pick if a judge asks. It costs you one clause and buys the whole figure's credibility.

`writeup-full.pdf` keeps **both** charts — rebased first, then the un-rebased record — since it has room to show the hole as well as the recovery.

Fitting the bigger figure cost the "beaten on the thing we understood best" bullet. Page 1 already tells that story in full as the Game 62 cliff, so nothing was lost.

## Still outstanding

The **97-Game refresh** hasn't reported yet. Everything currently on page 2 and in the deck — *"2 losing Games in the last twenty, worst 3,941"*, *"mean-to-σ 0.72, second in the field"*, *"four in the last thirty, fewest of any team"*, *"seven teams worse than −80,000"*, and the rebased **+394,108 / 2nd of 17** — is computed at **94 Games**. Three more have settled.

If you need to upload before it lands, the figures are defensible as-is provided you say "as of Game 94". I'll apply the diff to both PDFs and the deck the moment it reports, and I'll flag loudly if any of those superlatives broke.
